MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS

(a) to (e) Providing Piped Natural Gas (PNG) connections is part of the development of City Gas 
Distribution (CGD) Network, which inter alia include creation of pipeline infrastructure and other 
facilities for the supply of PNG to domestic, commercial and industrial units. This is being carried out

of 12/12A CGD bidding round, PNGRB has authorized entities for the development of CGD network 
in 309 Geographical Areas (GAs), covering the entire mainland area of the country. As on 
31.05.2026, the authorized CGD entities have provided 1,70,69,775 PNG (D) connections across the 
country against the Minimum Work Programme (MWP) targets of 12,65,41,862 PNG (D) connections 
to be achieved by 2034. CGD infrastructure rollout is undertaken by the authorized entities in 
accordance with the authorization granted by PNGRB and the approved project plan. The GA-wise 
and state/UT wise PNG (D) connections progress, as on 31.05.2026, is at Annexure-I and Annexure-
II respectively. 
As informed by authorized CGD entities, challenges in achieving MWP primary include: 
(i) High capital investment requirements for development of CGD infrastructure, particularly 
in sparsely populated and remote areas. 

(ii) Delay in obtaining statutory permissions/Right of Use (RoU)/Right of Way (RoW) and 
other approvals from various Central, State and local authorities for laying pipelines and 
establishing CNG stations. 
(iii) Land availability for installation of CNG stations, City Gate Stations (CGS) and other 
associated infrastructure. 
(iv) Availability and timely connectivity to the Natural Gas pipeline network, especially in 
areas where trunk pipeline infrastructure is under development. 
(v) Geographical and terrain-related constraints, including hilly, forest, coastal and difficult-
to-access areas, which increase project complexity and cost. 
To accelerate the expansion of PNG Domestic connections across the country, PNGRB launched the 
National PNG Drive 2.0 from 1st January 2026 to 30th June 2026, during which 13,37,911 active 
PNG (Domestic) connections were added across the country. 
The progress of CGD networks is monitored regularly through reports submitted by CGD entities. In 
cases of delay or shortfall, entities are advised to take corrective measures. This includes convening 
progress review meetings or statutory hearings, as provided under applicable regulations, to discuss 
challenges and review the latest status of Minimum Work Programme (MWP) targets in their 
authorized GAs and issuance of notices to defaulting entities directing compliance with the terms and 
conditions of authorization and informing them of regulatory action, including penalties, in case of 
continued default. Additionally, the Government holds regular interactions and meetings with State

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

ELECTRIFIED VILLAGES IN RAJASTHAN 
 
†2004. SHRI BRIJENDRA SINGH OLA: 
 
 Will the Minister of POWER 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the total number of villages declared electrified by the Government in the 
country so far along with the district -wise details for the State of Rajasthan 
particularly regarding the status of backward areas;  
 
(b) whether the Government has conducted any surve y or inquiry in such 
declared electrified villages to ascertain families/households still without an 
electricity connection despite the presence of electricity poles, transformers 
or sub-stations, if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor;  
 
(c) the concrete steps being taken by the Government to ensure that the 
electricity reaches every household in those villages where some families are 
still without power; and  
 
(d) whether the Government proposes to initiate any inquiry and verificatio n 
mechanism in this regard so that electrification on paper translates into 
electricity actually reaching households and if so, the details thereof including 
timeline for the same? 
A N S W E R 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER  
 
(SHRI SHRIPAD NAIK)  
 
(a) to (d): Electricity being a concurrent subject, supply and distribution of 
electricity to all consumers is within the purview of the respective State 
Government/ distribution utility. Government of India (GoI) has been 
supplementing the effort s of the States through various schemes to help 
achieve the objective of providing quality and reliable supply of power to all 
consumers. 
 
 As reported by the States/ UTs, all the inhabited un -electrified census 
villages in the country have been electrified.  A total of 18,374 villages were 
electrified under Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana (DDUGJY) launched 
in 2014, including 427 villages in the State of Rajasthan ( District wise details 
enclosed at Annexure-I). Under DDUGJY and thereafter during Pradhan  Mantri 
Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana (SAUBHAGYA) launched in October, 2017, all willing 
households as reported by the States/ UTs were electrified. A total of 2.86 crore 
households were electrified during SAUBHAGYA period including 21,27,728 
households in t he State of Rajasthan. Both the schemes stand closed as on 
31.03.2022. 
 

 Under ongoing Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS) launched in 
2021, grid electrification works amounting to Rs. 6,521 crore have been 
sanctioned for 13.65 lakh households, base d on proposal submitted by the 
States post survey, including works for electrification of households belonging 
to Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group (PVTG) identified under Pradhan Mantri 
Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN), tribal households under DA-
JGUA (Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan), households belonging to 
Scheduled Caste (SC) under Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana 
(PM-AJAY) and households in remote & border areas under Vibrant Villages 
Program (VVP), wherever found feasible (state-wise details are at Annexure–II). 
This includes Rs 1,765 crore sanctioned for electrification of 4.39 lakh 
households in the state of Rajasthan. Out of the sanction at country level, a 
total of 4.87 lakh households have been electrifie d till date including 
approximately 1.31 lakh households in the State of Rajasthan (District wise 
details are enclosed at Annexure-III). 
 
Government of India is taking all necessary steps to support States for 
electrification of all households. Since most of the left -out households are in 
remote, hilly and forest areas, the norms for electrification under RDSS were 
relaxed and the ceiling limit for cost of electrification was enhanced. Grid based 
electrification works have been sanctioned under RDSS whereve r found 
feasible as per the revised norms, based on proposals submitted by the States.  
 
Further, Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) is implementing 
the New Solar Power Scheme (for PVTG and Tribal Habitations/Villages) under 
PM-JANMAN and DAJGUA w hich includes electrification of un -electrified 
households (HHs) in PVTG and Tribal habitations/villages in identified tribal 
habitations/villages through off -grid solar systems; where electricity supply 
through grid is not techno-economically feasible.  
 
Under this scheme, as on 30.06.2026, 11,838 households have been 
electrified through solar off -grid systems in ten states. State -wise details are

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA  
MINISTRY OF JAL SHAKTI 
DEPARTMENT OF DRINKING WATER & SANITATION 
  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2005 
 ANSWERED ON 30/07/2026 
IMPLEMENTATION OF JJM AND JJM 2.0 IN VALSAD 
 
2005. SHRI DHAVAL LAXMANBHAI PATEL: 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state: 
(a) the present status of implementation of Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) and JJM 2.0 in Valsad 
Lok Sabha Constituency including coverage of households with functional tap water 
connections; 
(b) the details of water supply schemes, bulk pipelines and infrastructure works completed or 
underway thereof; 
(c) the progress under Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari Abhiyan and Jal Shakti Abhiyan: Catch the 
Rain in Gujarat including the number of water conservation structures created such as borewell 
recharge with community and CSR participation; and 
(d) whether any assessment has been made regarding groundwater recharge and water body 
rejuvenation in Gujarat and if so, the details thereof? 
  
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI 
(SHRIV. SOMANNA) 
 
(a) & (b) Drinking Water is a ‘State’ subject, and hence, under Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM), the 
responsibility of planning, approval, implementation, operation & maintenance of drinking 
water supply schemes lies with State/UT Governments. The Government of India supports the 
States by providing technical and financial assistance. 
Since August 2019, Government of India, in partnership with States/UTs including Gujarat, is 
implementing JJM – Har Ghar Jal to make provision of tap water supply to every rural 
household of the country. The Union Cabinet has approved extension of the JJM up to 
December 2028, with an enhanced outlay and a restructured implementation framework 
focusing on structural reforms in the rural drinking water supply sector under JJM 2.0. 
As reported by State of Gujarat, as on date, all rural households have been provided with tap 
water connection including those in Valsad Lok Sabha constituency. As numerous projects are 

Page 2 of 6 
 
implemented concurrently at various levels across the States/UTs for achieving the envisaged 
objectives of JJM, project -wise details of individual projects/ schemes for rural water supply 
projects are maintained at the State Government level. 
(c) As informed by the Department of Water Resources, River Development & Gang a 
Rejuvenation, water is a State subject and States are primarily responsible for planning, funding 
and implementing water conservation measures, while the Central Government supplements 
these efforts. 
The Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari (JSJB) initiative was launched on 6 September 2024 to promote 
community-led, low-cost rainwater harvesting through recharge structures such as borewells, 
recharge shafts and pits, supported by community contributions, CSR and convergence with 
Central, State and local schemes. JSJB 2.0 was implemented from 1 June 2025 to 31 May 2026, 
and JSJB: Catch the Rain (CTR)–2026 was launched on 1 June 2026 by integrating JSJB with 
the Jal Shakti Abhiyan: Catch the Rain (JSA: CTR) campaign. District-wise progress in Gujarat 
under JSJB 1.0 and 2.0 is at Annexure-I. 
The Jal Shakti Abhiyan (JSA), launched in 2019 and expanded nationwide as JSA: Catch the 
Rain in 2021 with the message "Catch the Rain: Where It Falls, When It Falls," has evolved 
into a national water conservation campaign with annu al thematic focus. Since 2023, the 
campaign has targeted priority districts for source sustainability, groundwater management and 
community participation. JSA: CTR 2025, themed "Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari: Jan Jagrukta 
Ki Or," focused on grassroots particip ation, convergence and innovative financing in 148 
CGWB-identified districts. District -wise progress in Gujarat under JSA: CTR 2025 is at 
Annexure-II. 
(d) As informed by DoWR, GR & RD, Dynamic Ground Water Resources of the country 
including Gujarat are assessed every year jointly by the Central Ground Water Board (CGWB) 
and the State Government. The annual ground water resource assessment provides updated 
estimates of annual groundwater recharge, annual extractable groundwater resources, annual 
groundwater extraction and stage of groundwater extraction and categorizes assessment units 
as Safe, Semi -Critical, Critical and Over -Exploited based on the stage of groundwater 
extraction. A comparison of the Ground Water Resource Assessments for 2017 and 2025 in 
Gujarat indicates that during this period, the Total Annual Ground Water Recharge increased 
from 22.37 BCM to 27.58 BCM, while the Annual Extractable Ground Water Resource 
increased from 21.25 BCM to 25.61 BCM. Although the Annual Ground Water Extraction 
increased from 13.58 BCM to 14.33 BCM, the Stage of Ground Water Extraction declined 
from 63.89% to 55.95%, mainly due to the increase in groundwater recharge and extractable 
resources.

Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of studies conducted by the Government regarding the water footprint 
associated with ethanol production from sugarcane, maize, paddy and other feedstocks, the 
implications thereof for groundwater resources, irrigation demand, agricultural sustainability 
and water security, with specific reference to Tamil Nadu;  
(b)  the comparative assessment available regarding water consumption, ethanol yield and 
environmental sustainability of various feedstocks used under the Ethanol Blended Petrol 
Programme;  
(c)  the measures adopted/proposed by the Government for encouraging water-efficient 
feedstocks, utilisation of agricultural residues, second-generation biofuels and other 
sustainable alternatives for ethanol production; 
(d)  the details of funds allocated, released and utilised by the Government under ethanol- 
blending, biofuel development and related infrastructure programmes during the last five 
years, year-wise; and 
(e)  the safeguards adopted by the Government to balance energy security objectives with 
concerns relating to food security, water conservation and sustainable agricultural practices? 
ANSWER

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS  
 (SHRI SURESH GOPI) 
(a) to (e):  An expert committee was constituted in 2024 by Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers 
Welfare to examine the water consumption of various ethanol feedstock crops. The Report has found 
that water requirement is maximum for Rice followed by Maize and Sugarcane.  
The Government has adopted a balanced approach to the Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme, 
ensuring that water sustainability, food security and farmers' interests remain paramount. 
The Government follows a diversified feedstock strategy under the National Policy on Biofuels. 
Ethanol is produced from multiple approved feedstocks, including sugarcane-based feedstocks, 
maize, damaged foodgrains, broken rice, foodgrains unfit for human consumption, surplus 
foodgrains approved by the National Biofuel Coordination Committee (NBCC) and other approved 
agricultural feedstocks. The Government is also promoting Second Generation (2G) ethanol from 
agricultural residues under the Pradhan Mantri JI-VAN Yojana to progressively increase the use of 
non-food feedstocks. 
The diversion of foodgrains for ethanol production is carefully calibrated in consultation with the 
Department of Food & Public Distribution and other concerned Ministries. Food security, Public 

Distribution System (PDS) requirements, National Food Security Act (NFSA) obligations, Other 
Welfare Schemes (OWS) and prescribed buffer stocks are accorded the highest priority. Only 
surplus foodgrains, after meeting these requirements, are permitted for ethanol production. The 
Government is also promoting crop diversification towards comparatively less water-intensive 
feedstocks such as maize and encouraging sustainable agricultural practices so that expansion of 
ethanol feedstocks remains balanced with the production of pulses, oilseeds and other essential food 
crops. 
Water-use efficiency is also being enhanced through micro-irrigation, drip irrigation and other water 
conservation measures under the Per Drop More Crop component of the Pradhan Mantri Krishi 
Sinchayee Yojana. Many sugar mills are also encouraging farmers to adopt water-efficient 
cultivation practices. 
Molasses-based distilleries with incineration boilers and grain-based distilleries are required to

Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) whether the Government has assessed the impact of the evolving security situation and 
armed conflicts in the West Asia/Gulf region on international operations of Indian airlines 
and if so, the details thereof; 
 
(b) the details of flights rerouted, diverted or cancelled by Indian carriers due to airspace 
restrictions during the last two years, year-wise; 
 
(c) whether the resultant airspace restrictions, route diversions and security advisories have 
affected flight schedules, operational costs, passenger traffic and airfares on services operated 
by Indian carriers to Europe, North America and the Gulf region and if so, the details thereof; 
 
(d) whether the Government has conducted any assessment of the economic impac t of such 
disruptions on the Indian civil aviation sector including airlines and air cargo operations and 
if so, the details thereof; and 
 
(e) the measures taken by the Government in coordination with the relevant national and 
international agencies to ensure the safety of passengers and crew, maintain uninterrupted air 
connectivity and mitigate the operational and financial impact on Indian airlines? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION      (Shri Murlidhar 
Mohol) 
(a) and (b): The Gov ernment continuously monitored the situation in the West Asia/Gulf 
region. Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) has issued advisories to address and 
ensure the safety of passengers, crew, and aircraft evolving from the risks arising from the 
West A sia conflict. These advisories provide operational guidance on affected airspace, 
including Notice to Airmen (NOTAM), identification of high -risk areas, Flight Information 
Region (FIR) boundaries and impacted countries, enabling operators to plan safe routing after 
conducting comprehensive Safety Risk Assessments. 
 
(c) to (e) : Indian carriers have informed that re -routing of flights has led to increased flight 
durations and higher fuel consumption, resulting in additional operational costs for airlines. 
The extent of such costs depends on route diversion, duration and prevailing fuel prices. 

Further, as informed, airlines are incurring significant revenue losses due to the ongoing 
crisis. Airlines are, however, taking necessary measures to mitigate the impact while ensuring 
continuity of operations. 
; 
A 24*7 Passenger Assistance Control Room was established for real -time coordination and 
passenger support. Passenger assistance was also provided through airport help desks and 
real-time travel updates by airli nes. The Ministry also worked closely with the Ministry of 
External Affairs to address emerging requirements relating to Indian carriers and Indian 
nationals in the region. The Indian Mission in Riyadh, in coordination with Indian Missions 
in Bahrain, Iraq , Kuwait, Oman, Qatar and the UAE, facilitated the transit of affected 
individuals through Saudi Arabia.

             SMT BHARTI PARDHI                       
             SHRI RAVINDRA DATTARAM WAIKAR            
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) whether the Government has review ed the Fit -to-Fly medical criteria to include 
comprehensive mental health assessments for holders of Commercial Pilot Licences (CPLs); 
 
(b) if so, the details thereof including the mandatory Peer Support Programmes that airlines 
are required to establish to address pilot burnout; 
 
(c) the mechanism in place for non -punitive reporting of stress -related issues by crew 
members without fear of immediate suspension of licence; 
 
(d) the details of the study conducted by the Directorate General of Civil Aviation ( DGCA) 
on the impact of Ultra -Long Haul flights on the circadian rhythm and mental alertness of 
cockpit crew; 
 
(e) the steps taken to prevent commercial pressure from airlines that may compel pilots to 
operate flights despite reporting fatigue; and 
 
(f) the total number of pilots who have successfully availed departmental counselling services 
since the implementation of the new Flight Duty Time Limitations (FDTL) norms? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION      (Shri Murlidhar 
Mohol) 
(a) to (c): Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) vide Medical Circular 01/2023 has 
issued guidelines for Mental Health Promotion of Flight Crew and Air Traffic Control 
Officers (ATCOs). Comprehensive Mental Health Assessment is already a fitness cr iteria to 
obtain medical fitness and all DGCA licences. Assessment of mental health of aircrews is 
conducted as a part of DGCA Medical Examinations on a regular basis. .; 
; 
DGCA undertakes quarterly review of all activities undertaken by major operators to wards 
promotion of mental health.; 

; 
Multiple measures are recommended to ensure availability of timely professional assistance. 
Operators are advised to help aircrews in capacity building through mental health awareness 
seminars, regular training sessions.; 
; 
Peer support program is a non-punitive and proactive program embedded in Medical Circular 
01 of 2023 for promotion of mental health and to assist aircrew in recognizing, coping up and 
overcoming various problems. This program is enshrined with the mec hanism for redressal 
without the fear of loosing any licence privileges upon disclosure of problems. Operators are 
implementing this program in letter and spirit to address pilot burnout and to ensure flight 
safety.; 
; 
(d): No study on such impact was conducted.; 
; 
(e) & (f): Fatigue reports are an important tool for identifying and mitigating crew fatigue. 
DGCA CAR 7/J/III mandates each operator to establish a clear policy on fatigue reporting

responsibility for fatigue management defined by the operator. 
 
As per the said CAR, all fatigue reports and action-taken reports are to be retained for at least 
one year and made available to DGCA when required. In addition, quarterly  fatigue reports, 
along with analysis and actions taken, is to be submitted to DGCA by the Head of

entries.t: FASTag Annual Plan
entries.head:
1 
 
  GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2017 
ANSWERED ON 30th JULY, 2026 
FASTAG ANNUAL PLAN 
†2017. SHRI LALJI VERMA: 
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
(a) the total number of FASTag users currently registered in the country; 
(b) the number of such users covered under the FASTag annual plan of 
Rs. 3,075; 
(c) the number of toll plazas being closed due to the provision of the 
distance of less than sixty kms. on the same route, State-wise; and 
(d) whether the Government has fixed any specific timeline for complete 
replacement of  physical toll plazas across the country with satellite -
based GNSS and automatic number plate  recognition technology to 
enable distance-based toll collection? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
(a) As on June, 2026, about 6.23 crore FASTags  are active across the 
country and are used for electronic toll transactions at National Highway 
fee plazas.  
(b) Annual Pass scheme for non -commercial cars, jeeps, and vans has 
come into effect from 15 th August, 2025. As of June, 2026, more than 77 
lakh Annual Passes have been issued registering 63 crore transactions 

2 
 
on National Highway Fee Plazas. Presently, around 33% of total 
Electronic Toll Collection (ETC) transactions done by car/jeep/van are 
Annual Pass Transactions.  
(c) Fee plazas are established on National Highways as per the 
provisions of the National Highways Fee (Determination of Rates and 
Collection) Rules, 2008, wherein Sub -Rule (2) of Rule 8, stipulates that 
any other fee plaza on the same section of National Highway and in the 
same direction are not   established within a distance of 60 km. Further 
the proviso to the said Rule also states that where the executing 
authority deems necessary, it may for reasons to be recorded in writing, 
establish or allow to establish another fee plaza within a distance of 60 
km. 
For cases having less inter distance between fee plaza, the location of 
fee plaza  is examined by a Committee  as per the provisions of NH Fee 
Rules 2008,  considering all local factors and other nearby National 
Highways for making a reco mmendation to the competent 
authority regarding publication of fee notification in the Gazette of India 
and the commencement of fee collection. 
(d) The Apex Committee and High -Level Empowered Committee 
consisting of Experts from Industry and Academia, in view of security 
and privacy considerations, breach and overall operational control, have 
recommended further deliberations for satellite -based GNSS tolling 
system.  
However, in order to enhance toll operations and enable seamless 
movement of vehicles, the Government has adopted a phased rollout of 
Multi-Lane Free Flow (MLFF) user fee collection on 4 -lane and above 
National Highways, based on the outco mes and efficacy of the awarded 
projects. Under the MLFF tolling system, gantry -mounted high -
performance Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) readers and 
Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) cameras are used for the 
deduction of user fees through the  existing FASTag system. This 
facilitates barrier -less tolling, wherein user fees are collected from 

3 
 
vehicle users without requiring them to stop, slow down, or remain in a 
designated lane.  
Multi-Lane Free Flow based barrier less tolling using existing FA STag 
(RFID)+ANPR/AI- Technology has been awarded on 17 fee plazas. Out of 
17 awarded fee plazas, 05 fee plazas have already gone Live i.e., 
Choryasi Fee Plaza (Surat, Gujarat); Mundka Fee Plaza (Delhi); Gharaunda 
Fee Plaza (Haryana); Manoharpura Fee Plaza (Rajasthan); Daulatpura Fee 
Plaza (Rajasthan). Additional 104 fee plazas have been identified for 
barrier less tolling mechanism under MLFF.

The scheme has four verticals namely, Beneficiary -led individual house

 Will the Minister of POWER

(a) to (f) :  Ujjwal DISCOM Assurance Yojana (UDAY) was launched in 2015 with 
an overall objective of operational and financial turnaround of State -owned 
distribution utilities through financial restructuring and efficiency improvements in 
distribution sector. UDAY envisaged States taking over 75% of the outstanding debt 
of the DISCOMs, as on 30.09.2015, by issuing SDL (State Development Loan) Bonds.

As a result of participation of DISCOMs under UDAY and various other 
reform measures undertaken thereafter by the Central and State Governments, the 
Aggregate Technical and Commercial (AT&C) losses at national level have reduced 
from 25.72% in FY15 to 15.04% in FY25 while the gap between Average Cost of 
Supply and Average Revenue Realized (ACS-ARR) has narrowed from Rs. 0.58/kWh 
to Rs. 0.06/kWh. These collective efforts have also resulted in distribution utilities, 
on an aggregate basis, achieving a profit after tax (PAT) of Rs 2,701 crore in FY25

entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF POWER 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.2032 
ANSWERED ON 30.07.2026 
 
PROGRESS MADE UNDER RDSS 
 
2032. SHRI YADUVEER WADIYAR: 
 
 Will the Minister of POWER 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the progress made under the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS) 
in reducing Aggregate Technical and Commercial (AT&C) losses across the 
country;  
 
(b) the targets fixed under the said scheme for reduction of AT&C losses and 
the current achievement levels, State-wise including Karnataka;  
 
(c) the funds sanctioned and released under RDSS to Karnataka for feeder 
separation, smart metering and infrastructure strengthening; and  
 
(d) the measurable impact of RDSS interventions on improving operational 
efficiency and financial sustainability of DISCOMs? 
 
A N S W E R 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER  
 
(SHRI SHRIPAD NAIK)  
 
(a) to (d): Government of India (GoI) launched the Revamped Distribution 
Sector Scheme (RDSS) in July 2021 with the objective of improving the 
quality and reliability of power supply to consumers through a financially 
sustainable and operationally efficient dist ribution sector. The Scheme 
has an outlay of Rs. 3,03,758 crore with an estimated Central Grant of Rs. 
97,631 crore. The Scheme aims at reducing the Aggregate Technical and 
Commercial (AT&C) losses to pan-India levels of 12-15%. 
Under the Scheme, financial  assistance is being provided to the 
distribution utilities (excluding private sector utilities) for undertaking 
loss reduction infrastructure works and smart metering works. Projects 
worth Rs. 1.53 lakh crore for loss reduction infrastructure works and Rs. 
1.31 lakh crore for smart metering works have been sanctioned under the 
Scheme. 

The following works have been sanctioned under the Scheme to 
strengthen the distribution network and reduce AT&C losses: 
 
 Creation of new substations and upgradation of exist ing 
substations. 
 Installation of new Distribution Transformers (DTs) and 
augmentation of existing DTs. 
 Replacement of old conductors. 
 Agriculture feeder segregation works. 
 IT/OT systems like Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition 
(SCADA) to improve grid monitoring. 
 Smart metering works covering 19.79 crore consumers, 2.11 lakh 
feeders and 52.53 lakh DTs. Smart metering works help in improving 
the billing efficiency of utilities through automated energy 
accounting, which enables identification of leakages and high-loss 
areas, and in improving the collection efficiency of utilities through 
the pre-paid system. 
The release of funds under the Scheme is contingent upon 
improvement in the operational and financial performance of the 
distribution utilities. This, in addition to other initiatives taken by GoI, has 
helped in bringing discipline in the payment of Government subsidies and 
Government department dues to the utilities, regular issuance of tariff 
orders, publishing of accounts, non-creation of regulatory assets, etc. 
With the concerted efforts of the Central and State Governments 
and as a result of the reform measures undertaken, AT&C losses across 
the country have reduced from 21.91% in FY21 to 15.04% in FY25. 
Further, the gap between the Average Cost of Supply (ACS) and the 
Average Revenue Realised (ARR) has reduced from Rs. 0.69/kWh in FY21 
to Rs. 0.06/kWh in FY25. Distribution Utility wise details of AT&C losses 
and targets prescribed under RDSS are enclosed in Annexure. 
As regards Karnataka, the State has not availed assistance under 
RDSS for loss reduction and smart metering works. However, household 
electrification works worth Rs. 45 crore (GBS: 27 crore), covering 
electrification of 6,903 households, have been sanctioned for Karnataka, 
as per the proposal submitted by the State. Out of this, 3,260 households 
have been electrified and Rs 10.14 crore have been released, till date.

Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has recently reduced the price of commercial LPG cylinders by 
about one hundred and eighty-three rupees per cylinder and has left domestic LPG refill 
prices unchanged, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether the international crude oil prices have declined to levels prevailing prior to the 
recent geopolitical conflict in West Asia; 
(c) if so, the quarter-wise details of crude oil prices at which India purchased crude oil from 
the international market during the last two years; and 
(d) whether the Government proposes to review domestic LPG prices in view of the easing of 
international crude oil prices, if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS 
 (SHRI SURESH GOPI) 
(a) to (d): Prices of LPG in the country are linked to Saudi CP, the benchmark for LPG 
prices in international market. Government continues to review and modulate the effective 
price to consumer for domestic LPG only.  
With the onset of the West Asia crisis, the average Saudi CP (the international benchmark for 
LPG pricing) rose upto US$ 780/MT in April and May 2026. In June 2026, as the Saudi CP 
rose further to US$ 796/MT (excluding premium), the Market Determined Price (MDP) of a 
14.2 kg domestic LPG cylinder went to Rs.1,695 per 14.2 Kg cylinder.  
The Retail Selling Price (RSP) of domestic LPG has been maintained at Rs. 942 per 14.2 kg 
cylinder. At this price, there is an implicit subsidy (under-recovery) of over Rs. 500 per 14.2 
kg cylinder as of July 2026; the corresponding under-recovery exceeded Rs. 700 per 14.2 kg 
cylinder in June 2026. For more than 10.5 crore PMUY consumers, the effective price is only 
Rs. 642 per cylinder (Delhi), after a targeted subsidy of Rs. 300 per cylinder, in addition to 
the implicit subsidy of more than Rs 500 per cylinder. 
On the other hand, Public Sector Oil Marketing Companies (PSU OMCs) and private sector 
LPG marketing companies are free to determine the prices of commercial LPG based on 
prevailing international market prices and market conditions. Accordingly, the Retail Selling 
Price of 19 kg commercial LPG cylinders is revised and declared by the OMCs on a monthly 
basis, without any Government intervention. The Retail Selling Price (RSP) of a 19 kg 
commercial LPG cylinder was  revised in June 2026 to Rs. 2,930.00 by the Oil Marketing 
Companies in July 2026. 
Even the crude oil prices were USD 69/barrel in February 2026 prior to the crisis and

entries.head:
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 2041 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 30th July, 2026 
ETHANOL BLENDING AND ITS PRODUCTION COST 
 
2041. DR. T SUMATHY ALIAS THAMIZHACHI THANGAPANDIAN: 
 
पेĚोͧलयम और Ĥाकृ Ǔतक गैस मंğी 
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Union Government has taken serious note of the adverse effects of ethanol 
blending and the escalation in its cost, if so, the details thereof; and 
(b)  whether it is true that the cost of production of one litre of petrol is lower than the cost of 
production of one litre of ethanol, if so, the details thereof along with the valid reasons for 
the Government to promote ethanol-blended petrol for vehicles and to adhere to the Ethanol 
Blended Petrol Programme? 
ANSWER 
पेĚोͧलयम और Ĥाकृ Ǔतक गैस मंğालय मɅ राÏय मंğी 
(Įी सुरेश गोपी) 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS  
 (SHRI SURESH GOPI) 
(a) & (b): The Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme has been implemented through a 
phased, scientifically validated and consultative process involving NITI Aayog, automobile 
manufacturers, Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs), Automotive Research Association of India 
(ARAI), Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM), Indian Institute of Petroleum (IIP) 
and other technical institutions. 
Ethanol is not a new fuel. It has been used globally for over a century, with countries such as Brazil 
operating higher ethanol blends for decades. In India, the Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme 
commenced with a pilot in 2001, E5 was introduced in 2006, and although blending remained 
around 1.53% in 2013-14, it has since been increased progressively in a calibrated manner after 
creating the necessary production capacity, infrastructure and regulatory framework. 
 
The rollout of higher ethanol blends was undertaken only after extensive consultation with 
automobile manufacturers, SIAM, ARAI, component manufacturers, testing agencies and Oil 
Marketing Companies (OMCs). Extensive laboratory studies and field trials conducted by ARAI, 
SIAM, IOCL, IIP and automobile manufacturers covering parameters such as engine durability, 
drivability, startability, corrosion resistance, material compatibility, emissions and fuel efficiency 
have confirmed that E20 is safe for use under prescribed standards. 
These studies also established that legacy vehicles do not exhibit any significant variation in 
performance or abnormal wear and tear due to E20. These extensive laboratory studies, field 
validation and real-world operating experience have not established any widespread adverse impact 
on vehicle performance due to E20 fuel. 

The Government's assessment is based not only on laboratory research but also on large-scale 
experience after nationwide implementation. India witnesses approximately 8 crore vehicles visiting 
retail outlets every day (around 80% petrol vehicles). 
This is evident from the fact that E15+ blended petrol has been in widespread use for over three-and-
a-half years and E19-E20 fuel for over two-and-a-half years. More than 20 crore two-wheelers and 
over 3 crore petrol cars have been operating on these blends without any verified evidence of 
widespread engine failure or vehicle breakdown attributable to ethanol blending. Manufacturer 
service data confirm that there is no abnormal corrosion, wear or reduction in vehicle life due to E20 
fuel. Manufacturers continue to honour warranty obligations for vehicles using E20 fuel, providing 
further confidence in its safety and reliability. 
A leading OEM serviced 2.84 crore vehicles during FY 2025-26, including approximately 1.5 crore

FLIGHTS FROM HISAR AIRPORT

be pleased to state:- 
(a) whether the Government proposes to operate new flights under the UDAN 
Scheme to expand air connectivity from Hisar Airport/Aerodrome in Haryana to 
major cities in the country and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the details of the flights cur rently operating and proposed from Hisar Airport 
along with their destinations and operational status; 
(c) the amount of the funds sanctioned and utilised so far under the UDAN Scheme 
for the development of Hisar Airport including expansion of passenger fa cilities, 
runway, terminal building and other essential infrastructure; and 
(d) whether the Government has prepared any special action plan to develop Hisar 
as a regional aviation hub and attract new airlines and if so, the details thereof and 
the likely timeline fixed in this regard? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION       
(Shri Murlidhar Mohol) 
(a) to (d): The Government has launched the next phase of the UDAN Scheme on 
04.07.2026 to further enhance regional air connectivity across the country, connect 
120 new destinations, and serve 4 crore passengers over the next 10 years. As per 
the provisions of the Scheme, Hisar airport is eligible for bidding under the 
underserved Airport category in the forthcoming bidding rounds. Further, t he

passenger demand and operational feasibility.

aviation has been deregulated. Airlines are free to induct capacity with any aircraft 
type, free to select  whatever markets and network they wish to service depending 
on their operational & commercial viability.

IMPACT OF CLIMATE CHANGES ON CHANGPA TRIBAL COMMUNITY IN 
LADAKH 
2049.   SHRI MOHMAD HANEEFA: 
Will the Minister of TRIBAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has assessed the impact of climate change, shrinking grazing 
pastures, changing snowfall patterns and declining livestock productivity on the livelihood 
and traditional nomadic lifestyle of the Changpa tribal community in Ladakh and if so, the 
details thereof; 
(b) the details of welfare and livelihood schemes being implemented for Changpa families 
during the last five years; 
(c) whether any special programme has been launched for pasture development, veterinary 
healthcare, mobile service delivery, education, housing and income enhancement of Changpa 
pastoralists and if so, the details thereof; 
(d) the details of funds released under various schemes of the Ministry of Tribal Affairs for 
the Changthang region during the last five years; and 
(e) the measures being taken to strengthen the long-term socio-economic resilience and 
preserve the traditional culture and livelihood of the Changpa community? 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR TRIBAL AFFAIRS 
(SHRI DURGADAS UIKEY) 
(a): The Ministry of Tribal Affairs has not undertaken any study to assess the impact of climate 
change, shrinking grazing pastures, changing snowfall patterns and declining livestock 
productivity on the livelihood and traditional nomadic lifestyle of the Changpa tribal 
community in Ladakh. 

(b): Changpa families, being members of a Scheduled Tribe, are eligible beneficiaries under 
the welfare and livelihood schemes implemented by this Ministry and other line 
Ministries/Departments during the last five years, including: 
(i) Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN); 
(ii) Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DAJGUA); 
(iii) Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS); 
(iv) Pre-Matric, Post-Matric and National Overseas Scholarships for Scheduled Tribe 
students; 
(v) Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission (PMJVM); 
(c): Yes. Under the umbrella of DAJGUA, targeted interventions have been taken up for 
remote tribal habitations including Mobile Medical Units; mobile network delivery; 
residential hostel facilities; pucca housing under PM-AWAS (Gramin) etc. Additionally, 
livelihood and income-enhancement support for Pashmina wool production, marketing 
linkages and value addition is being undertaken through TRIFED. 
(d): Under PMJVM scheme, TRIFED has released an amount of ₹15 lakhs for establishment

Electricity being a concurrent subject, the supp ly and distribution of 
electricity to the various categories of consumers/areas/districts in a State/UT 
is looked after by the respective Power Utility/State Government. Further, The 
Central Government supplements the efforts of the State Governments by 
establishing power plants through Central Public Sector Undertakings (CPSUs) 
and allocate power from them to the various States / UTs. 
 
To ensure generation capacity remains ahead of projected demand, all 
the States, in consultation with CEA, have prepared their “Resource Adequacy 
Plans (RAPs)”, which are dynamic 10 -year rolling plans and includes power 
generation as well as power procurement planning.

terms of Energy for the last three f inancial years and current year (upto June,

entries.t: Increase in Height of Culverts/Bridges
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
 LOK SABHA 
  UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2059 
   ANSWERED ON 30TH JULY, 2026   
INCREASE IN HEIGHT OF CULVERTS/BRIDGES 
2059. SHRI JAGADISH SHETTAR: 
  
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री 
 
 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether any measures are being contemplated to increase the 
height of culverts/bridges from the present 4.5 metres to 5.5 metres 
while undertaking construction of highways to facilitate easy 
movement of vehicles beneath them; and 
  
(b) if so, the details thereof? 
  
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI)  
 
(a) to (b) Culverts and bridges are cross -drainage structures on 
National Highways which facilit ate the drainage of natural 
watercourses across the National Highways. The vent size, span 
arrangement and height of such structures are governed by 
hydraulic considerations at the location, namely the design 
discharge, the highest flood level, the permiss ible afflux and scour 
considerations, and not by the requirement of movement of vehicles 
beneath the highway as they are meant for crossing of water 
channel. 

However, movement of traffic across and beneath a National 
Highway is  provided through grade -separated structures, namely 
Vehicular Underpasses (VUP), Light Vehicle Underpasses 
(LVUP)/Small Vehicle Underpasses (SVUP), Cattle Underpasses 
(CUP) and Pedestrian Underpasses (PUP). A minimum vertical 
clearance of 5.5 metres is already prescribed for Vehicula r 
Underpasses (VUP) on National Highways, and is provided while 
undertaking construction, four/six -laning and upgradation of 
National Highways. Structures falling in the LVUP/SVUP/CUP/PUP 
categories (height varying from 3.0 m to 4.5 m) are, by design, 
provided with lower vertical clearances, since they are intended to 
serve restricted categories of traffic including pedestrians.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF POWER 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.2063 
ANSWERED ON 30.07.2026 
 
REDUCTION IN TRANSMISSION AND DISTRIBUTION LOSSES 
 
†2063. SHRI MANSUKHBHAI DHANJIBHAI VASAVA: 
 
 Will the Minister of POWER 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the targets fixed for reducing transmission and distribution losses in the country 
during each of the last three years and the current year and the achievements made 
in this regard, State-wise;  
 
(b) whether the Government proposes to provide performance -linked incentives to 
the States for reducing transmission and distribution losses; and  
 
(c) if so, the details thereof? 
A N S W E R 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER  
 
(SHRI SHRIPAD NAIK)  
 
(a) to (c): The transmission losses in the country are around 3-4% on an annual basis. 
Distribution losses in the distribution network, along with the losses on account of 
shortfall in collection of revenue, are together reported as  Aggregate Technical & 
Commercial (AT&C) losses of the distribution utilities.  
 
Government of India (GoI) launched the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme 
(RDSS) in July 2021 with the objective of improving the quality of power through a 
financially sustainable and operationally efficient distribution sector. The scheme 
has an outlay of Rs. 3,03,758 crore and estimated Gross Budgetary Support (GBS) 
from Central Government of Rs. 97,631 crore.  
 
Under the scheme, financial assistance is being provided to th e distribution 
utilities for loss reduction infrastructure and smart metering works. Projects worth 
Rs. 1.53 lakh crore for loss reduction infrastructure and Rs. 1.31 lakh crore for smart 
metering works have been sanctioned under the scheme. Release of funds under the 
scheme is linked with performance of the distribution utilities against operational 
and financial parameters including the AT&C losses. Distribution utility wise AT&C 
loss reduction targets and achievements are enclosed at Annexure. 
 
With concerted efforts of the Central and State Governments and as a result 
of various reform measures undertaken, there has been a reduction in overall 
transmission and distribution losses. AT&C losses across the country have reduced 
from 21.91% in FY21 to 15.04% in FY25. These collective efforts have also resulted 
in distribution utilities, on an aggregate basis, achieving a profit after tax (PAT) of 
Rs 2,701 crore in FY25 for the first time since coming into force of Electricity Act, 
2003.

entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2064 
ANSWERED ON 30TH JULY, 2026 
  
PLANTATION OF TREES ALONG NHs 
  
2064. DR. SAMBIT PATRA: 
  
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
 
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री 
  
be pleased to state: 
  
(a) whether the Government has formulated any policy for planting 
trees and greening along sides of National Highways (NHs) in the 
country and if so, the details thereof; 
  
(b) the details of monitoring and inspection carried out for compliance 
with the targets of plantation and maintenance parameters on NHs; 
  
(c) whether any policy is being implemented by the Government for 
penalising or awarding the contractors for negligent behavior or 
excellent work in plantation on the National Highways (NHs) and if so, 
the details thereof; and 
  
(d) the details of the targets set and achievements made regarding 
plantation of trees on National Highways by National Highways 
Authority of India (NHAI) during the last three years, State/UT-wise? 
  
  
ANSWER  
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI)  
  

(a)   The Government has formulated the Green Highways 
(Plantation, Transplantation, Beautification and Maintenance) Policy, 
2015 for planting trees and greenery along and on the sides of National 
Highways (NHs). 
The policy deals with avenue and median plantation, landscaping, 
beautification and transplantation wherever feasible, along the NHs. It 
aims at environmental conservation, carbon sequestration, dust and 
noise reduction, enhancement of road safety and creation of 
employment opportunities. The policy provides for plantation of 
suitable indigenous species, maintenance of plantations for the 
prescribed period, involvement of agencies i ncluding government 
organizations, Non -Governmental Organizations (NGOs) and self -help 
groups, and use of technology-based monitoring. 
(b)  Plantation and maintenance works are monitored through a 
multi-tier mechanism. Project Directors/Implementation Unit s and 
Regional Offices carry out periodic inspections to verify plantation, 
survival rate and maintenance. 
Independent Engineers/Authority Engineers supervise compliance in 
projects where plantation forms part of civil contracts. Plantation 
progress is rev iewed periodically through review meetings with all 
stakeholders. 
(c)  ‘NHAI Green Highways Excellence Awards’ recognize exemplary 
plantation efforts based on survival rate, vigor, and adherence to 
standard specifications. Conversely, for negligent behavio r, strict 
penal provisions are enforced. 
In case of non -performance, poor maintenance or failure to achieve 
the prescribed survival percentage, contractual provisions provide for 
withholding of payments, recovery of costs, rectification at the 
contractor’s risk and cost, levy of contractual damages/penalties and 
other remedies as per the contract conditions. Payments are linked to 
successful establishment and maintenance of plantations. 
(d)  State/UT-wise details of plantation targets and achievements 
during the last three years are given at Annexure-I.

be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government proposes to exempt State owned public 
transport system from  remittance of toll on National Highway, if so, the 
details of action taken thereon; 
(b) whether the Union Government share the toll collected from NH-66 
with State considering  the share of State for land acquisition cost and 
GST exemption and if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether the Union Government examined the request of KSRTC for 
exempting from paying toll, if so, the details of action taken thereon; 
(d) whether the Government has considered the additional burden of Rs. 
two crores on  KSRTC per month for payment of toll, if so, the details 
thereof; 
(e) whether the Union Government considers the crisis of KSRTC, if so, 
the details thereof; and 
(f) whether the Union Government discourage the State owned public 
transport system, if so, the details of action taken to exempt KSRTC? 
 
  

2 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
(a) Provisions of National Highways Fee (Determination of Rates and 
Collection) Rules, 2008 are applicable on all types of transport vehicles 
including State Road Transport Corporations owned or  operated vehicles 
irrespective of its ownership.   
At present, there is no such proposal under co nsideration with 
Government to grant an exemption from the payment of user fees (Toll) 
to State owned public transport undertakings for the use of National 
Highways.   
(b) User fee at fee plazas on National Highways (NHs) is collected 
uniformly across the country in accordance with the provisions of the 
National Highways Fee (Determination of Rates and Collection) Rules, 
2008 and the respective Concession Agreements. The revenue collected 
by the Central Government from user fees on NHs, including those in 
Kerala, is deposited into the Consolidated Fund of India (CFI). Funds 
provided through budgetary allocations from the Consolidated Fund of 
India (CFI) are then utilized for the maintenance, development, and 
expansion of National Highways. 
  The contribution of the State Government of Kerala enabled projects 
in Kerala to be given higher priority despite the extremely high cost of 
Land Acquisition (LA) in the State. For development of NH 66 in Kerala, 
total Land Acquisition (LA) cost is about R s. 23,350 crore and 

3 
 
construction cost is about Rs. 28,370 crore. In the total cost, the 
contribution of the State government is Rs. 5,800 crore. 
  Further, there is an overall social and economic benefit to the local 
from the infrastructure development thr ough National Highways. Such 
development contributes to multiple advantages, including the 
expansion of towns and cities and broader economic growth within the 
State.  
(c) to (f) User fee for use of the section of National Highway is levied 
uniformly acros s all States as per the provisions of the NH Fee Rules 
including State Transport Undertaking buses. No blanket exemption from 
the payment of user fees has been provided to State Transport

There are already various p rovisions under the NH Fee Rules, that

सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री

(a) whether the Union Government is aware of the fact that various taxes 
at different rates are  being levied from the new vehicle buyer on the 
basis of vehicle size, engine capacity and fuel  type for passenger 
vehicles in addition to RTO registration fees and insurance premiums, if 
so, the details thereof; and 
(b) whether the Union Government has any proposal to stop collecting 
toll taxes and to  remove all toll plazas at all NHs across the country in 
view of the above, if so, the details thereof  and if not, the reasons 
therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
(a) As per Entry 57 of List II (State List) of the Seventh Schedule to the  
Constitution of India, the subject relating to taxes on vehicles, whether 
mechanically propelled or not, suitable for use on roads, including 
tramcars, subject to the provisions of Entry 35 of List III (Concurrent 
List), falls within the legislative compe tence of the States. Further, 
mechanically propelled vehicles, including the principles on which taxes 
on such vehicles are to be levied, comes under the List III (Concurrent 

2 
 
List). Therefore, taxes on motor vehicles fall within the sole jurisdiction 
of respective State /UT administration, in accordance with constitutional 
provisions. 
Further, the registration fee for motor vehicles is prescribed under Rule 
81 of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules (CMVR), 1989. 
(b) User fee at fee plaza is collected for the u se of a completed section 
of National Highway, uniformly across the country in accordance with 
the provisions of the National Highways Fee (Determination of Rates and 
Collection) Rules, 2008 and the respective Concession Agreements. 
As per the provisions o f National Highways Fee Rules, 2008, in case of 
concessionaire operated fee plaza, the fee notified as per concession 
agreement is collected by the concessionaire till the end of the 
concession period, and after the concession period is over, the fee Plaza  
is handed over to the Government and thereafter the fee is collected by 
the Central Government or the executing authority as per the fee 
specified under the provisions of NH Fee Rules, 2008.  In respect of fee 
plaza under public funded project, the fee le viable shall continue to be 
collected for such section of the National Highway. The revenue 
collected by the Central Government from user fee collection is 
deposited in Consolidated Fund of India (CFI) and the funds provided 
through budgetary allocation fr om the Consolidated Fund of India (CFI) 
are utilised for further maintenance, development and augmentation of 
National Highways.

entries.t: Progress under PMKSY
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2068 
ANSWERED ON 30TH JULY, 2026 
 
PROGRESS UNDER PMKSY 
 
2068. SMT. SANJNA JATAV: 
 
Will the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased to state: 
 
(a)   the progress made in development of modern food processing infrastructure and       
value-addition facilities under the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Sampada Yojana (PMKSY); 
(b) the number of projects sanctioned and completed along with the employment 
generated thereunder so far; 
(c) whether any project has been sanctioned under the said scheme in Bharatpur 
Parliamentary Constituency and if so, the details thereof including the present status 
of such project(s) and the number of persons provided employment after completion 
of the said Projects; 
(d) the steps taken to reduce post-harvest losses, promote Farmer Producer Organisations 
(FPOs) and enhance farmers’ income under the scheme; and 
(e) the impact of PMKSY on food processing capacity, exports and overall development 
of the food processing sector? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI CHIRAG PASWAN) 
 
(a) & (b): The Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MoFPI) has been implementing 
the Central Sector umbrella scheme Pradhan Mantri Kisan SAMPADA Yojana (PMKSY) 
across the country. The scheme aims to create modern food processing infrastructure 
and value addition facilities, enhance processing and preservation of agricultural produce, 
generate employment opportunities, and provide better remuneration to farmers. As on 
30.06.2026, a total of 1,735 projects have been approved under various component 
schemes of PMKSY, out of which 1,256 projects have been completed, creating 294.21 
LMT/Annum of processing and preservation capacity and generating 9.16 lakh 
employment opportunities across the country. 
 
(c): Pradhan Mantri Kisan SAMPADA Yojana (PMKSY) is demand driven in nature and 
applications are invited through Expression of Interest (EoI) from all over the country and 
funds are not allocated/sanctioned/released state-wise under any of the component 
schemes of PMKSY. The proposals received are scrutinized for their eligibility and 
evaluated based on the criteria fixed as per the extant scheme guidelines. Merit based 

approvals are given to the eligible proposals based on availability of funds. As on date, 
no project has been sanctioned under PMKSY in Bharatpur Parliamentary Constituency. 
 
(c) & (e): The component schemes under PMKSY provide financial assistance in the form 
of grants-in-aid/subsidy for creation of modern food processing and preservation 
infrastructure with the objective of reducing post-harvest losses and enhancing value 
addition. The creation of food processing infrastructure enhances demand for agricultural 
produce, leading to better price realization and improved income for farmers. PMKSY is a 
demand driven scheme and applications are invited from all eligible applicants, including 
Farmers Producing Organisation (FPOs) through Expression of Interest (EoI). To 
strengthen farmer–producer linkages, PMKSY provides enhanced financial assistance to 
FPOs along with relaxed eligibility conditions such as lower equity contribution, lower 
minimum bank loan requirement and a reduced net-worth requirement compared to the 
general category applicants. Further, Under the centrally sponsored PMFME scheme of the 
Ministry, FPOs are eligible for a 35% credit-linked subsidy up to ₹10 lakh for setting up or 
upgrading micro food processing enterprises, 35% grant of up to ₹3 crore for establishing 
Common Infrastructure and Branding & Marketing support in terms of grant upto 50% for 
groups of FPOs, at State/regional level. 
As on 30.06.2026, 1,256 projects have been completed under PMKSY, benefiting about 
37.76 lakh farmers and creating 294.21 LMT per annum of processing and preservation 
capacity, thereby strengthening the food processing ecosystem, promoting value addition, 
and contributing to the overall exports of food products and growth of the food processing 
sector.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF POWER

DEVELOPMENT OF PUMPED STORAGE PROJECTS IN ASSAM 
 
2069. SHRI AMARSING TISSO: 
 
 Will the Minister of POWER 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is promoting Pumped Storage Projects (PSPs) to 
facilitate renewable energy integration and meet peak electricity demand 
across the country and if so, the details thereof;  
 
(b) the number of Pumped Storage Projects under construction and at various 
stages of approval in the country, State-wise;  
 
(c) wheth er any Pumped Storage Project has been identified, proposed or is 
under examination in Assam, particularly in Karbi Anglong and Dima Hasao and 
if so, the details thereof; and  
 
(d) whether the Government provides any Central financial assistance or other 
incentives for the development of Pumped Storage Projects and if so, the details 
thereof? 
A N S W E R 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER  
 
(SHRI SHRIPAD NAIK)  
 
(a) & (d): The Government has undertaken the following measures to promote 
the development of Pumped Storage Projects (PSPs) in the country for 
facilitating renewable energy integration, enhancing grid flexibility, and 
meeting peak electricity demand: 
(i) Ministry of Power h as notified Guidelines to promote development of 
Pumped Storage Projects in the country on 10.04.2023. 
(ii) Budgetary Support towards Cost of Enabling Infrastructure, i.e., 
roads/bridges, railway sidings, ropeways, communication infrastructure and 
transmission line from power house to nearest pooling point.  
(iii) To provide a transparent, fair, standardized procurement framework based 
on open competitive bidding with appropriate risk -sharing between various 
stakeholders, MoP vide Gazette notification dated 06.02.2025 , has notified 
tariff based competitive bidding (TBCB) guidelines for procurement of 
storage capacity/stored energy from pumped storage plants.  
 

 
(iv) The Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (CERC), vide its Notification 
dated 26.06.2025, has provided for 100% waiver of Inter-State Transmission 
System (ISTS) charges for Pumped Storage Projects (PSPs) for a period of 
25 years from the Commercial Operation Date (COD), in respect of projects 
for which the construction work is awarded on or before 30.06.2028. 
(v) The Government of India, vide Gazette notification dated 01.08.2025, has 
revised the capital expenditure limit for schemes related to setting up hydro 
generating stations to ₹3,000 crore, requiring the concurrence of the Central 
Electricity Authority (CEA ). Further, the Government has exempted off -
stream closed-loop pumped storage schemes, irrespective of the quantum 
of capital expenditure, from the requirement of concurrence by the CEA. 
(vi) Central Electricity Authority (CEA) has revised Guidelines for formul ation 
and concurrence of Detailed Project Report (DPR) of PSPs. Under the revised 
guidelines, the timeline for concurrence of DPR has been reduced from 90 
days to 50 days for PSPs. Further, the clearance of Inter-State Aspects is not 
required for PSPs. 
(vii) Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change (MoEF&CC), vide its 
notification dated 18.05.2023, has enabled appraisal of PSPs under B2 
category subject to certain conditions.   
(viii) The MoEF&CC on 14.08.2023, has issued specific Terms of Reference (TOR) 
for the proposals involving off stream PSPs wherein collection of baseline 
data for one season (other than monsoon) is prescribed for off stream closed 
loop PSPs and collection of baseline data for two seasons (pre -monsoon & 
post-monsoon) is prescribed for off stream open loop PSPs. 
(ix) The MOEF&CC on 20.08.2024, has extended the provisions relating to survey 
in the forest areas for mining projects to other development projects 
including hydel/PSPs.  
(x) MOEF&CC vide letter dated 10.09.2025  has enhanced the number of 
boreholes for undertaking survey and explorations in the forest area for 
mining and developmental projects including hydel / PSPs. 
(b):  At present, 11 Pumped Storage Projects (PSPs) with a total installed 
capacity of 15,870 MW are under construction in the c ountry (Annexure -I). 
Further, 6 PSPs with an aggregate installed capacity of 8,140 MW have been 
concurred/appraised by the Central Electricity Authority (CEA) and are yet to be 
taken up for construction (Annexure -II). In addition, 1 PSP with an installed 
capacity of 640 MW is presently under examination in the CEA (Annexure-III).  
(c):   As per the records of the Central Electricity Authority (CEA), 6 Pumped 
Storage Projects (PSPs) with an aggregate installed capacity of 6,220 MW have 
been identified in the  State of Assam. Of these, 4 PSPs are at the Survey & 
Investigation (S&I) stage. The details are provided at Annexure-IV.
